title: Wffl app: choose the structure
question: Three ways to organise the same app, all native macOS, all in the website's type and palette. Lock the one that fits how you actually use Wffl.

options.label: Ask the library
options.lineage: Mindpalace's question-first home, Acme's prompt panel
options.thesis: Home is a question: search every word you have ever recorded, with your open action items beside it.
options.viewport: Native sidebar library; an ink search panel across the top of Home with recent queries; below it recent meetings as rich rows (left) and open action items across meetings (right). Matches underline in ember and jump to the timecode.
options.risk: Only pays off once the library has a few weeks of meetings in it.

options.label: Week ledger
options.lineage: Work OS's day numerals, a printed timetable
options.thesis: Home is your week, set like a timetable: big light day numerals, meetings in time order, decisions gathered on the right.
options.viewport: Native sidebar with a month strip; the week as rows under large day numerals (today marked in ember); each meeting a row with time, duration, speakers and waveform; a right inspector of this week's decisions and action items.
options.risk: Imported audio and old recordings feel secondary to the calendar.

options.label: Recorder dock
options.lineage: Voice Memos, Mantra's rich project cards
options.thesis: The recorder is always on screen: an ink dock with level, engine and permissions, and the library as a gallery of waveform cards below.
options.viewport: Ink dock across the top of the content with Record, live input level and readiness; a segmented filter (All, Recorded, Imported); meetings as cards with a waveform strip, speakers and decision count.
options.risk: The dock spends height on every screen, even when you are only reading.
